nodes.description: Discovery-to-planning-to-binding-to-verification flow, evidence boundaries, OCR fallback, memory, and optional API compatibility.

nodes.label: Page context and grounded intent

nodes.label: Natural language pipeline
nodes.description: English request interpretation, lexical/embedding retrieval, worker scheduling, queue verification, and private persistence policy.

nodes.label: Local observation and memory
nodes.description: Observation activation, private session retention, reusable knowledge limits, OCR masking, presentation storage, mock accounts, consent, and inactive analytics.

nodes.label: Trust and lifecycle boundaries
nodes.description: Untrusted evidence, host access, pinned sender/document identities, fresh binding, consequential review, outcome proof, and API protection.

nodes.label: Frontend ownership map
nodes.description: Application, feature, transport, presentation, widget, overlay, website practice, routing, and draft restoration responsibilities.

nodes.label: Extension implementation ownership
nodes.description: Stable entrypoints, one background session, content facade, shared local inference client, platform adapters, snapshot hooks and opt-in assistance ownership.

nodes.label: Passive guidance and accessible feedback
nodes.description: Noninteractive overlay geometry, polite panel announcements, focus management, user-controlled actions, and automated versus native accessibility evidence.

nodes.label: Shared presentation boundary
nodes.description: Shared guidance presentation and callbacks with no browser privileges, credentials, completion authority, or app-specific storytelling.

nodes.label: Website implementation ownership
nodes.description: Feature-local website state, controlled practice, canonical legal ownership, stable documentation aliases, mocked accounts, and consent boundaries.

nodes.label: Incremental live discovery
nodes.description: Cooperatively scans semantic/custom controls, open shadow roots, and authorized frames; retains up to 5,000 session controls while projecting at most 600 for planning.

nodes.label: Validated live observation
nodes.description: Bounded current control metadata includes structural context while geometry, state, eligibility, and risk remain independent of semantic identity.

nodes.label: Fresh eligible element binding
nodes.description: Document control IDs bind actual elements; changed meaning or recycled nodes invalidate signatures and binding. Only current eligible targets may be highlighted or scrolled.

nodes.label: Shared NavigationCore
nodes.description: Coordinates request interpretation, retrieval, grounded planning, queues, contextual workflows, visual fallback, and bounded return routing outside browser lifecycle/transport.

nodes.label: Persistent journey objective
nodes.description: Retains the destination independently of current controls, using verified transitions and documented milestones; future steps require live rebinding.

nodes.label: Evidence-based return routing
nodes.description: Uses observed dismissal controls, relevant task predecessors, or associated tabs without assuming forward operations are reversible.

nodes.label: Bounded recovery
nodes.description: Missing or insufficient evidence leaves the journey incomplete and triggers bounded recovery rather than an invented website route.
nodes.rationale: Unobserved and omitted controls do not prove route absence; an unsupported prediction cannot become an action.

nodes.label: Task-specific outcome verification
nodes.description: The extension verifies actual selected values, destinations, created items, deployment or membership states; wrong outcomes and unrelated toasts do not advance a task queue.

nodes.label: Low-evidence viewport OCR
nodes.description: Local Tesseract follows insufficient DOM evidence; full-image privacy masks apply before one bounded foreground menu/dialog pass and masked viewport fallback. Capture-space coordinates stay ephemeral and OCR cannot prove completion.

nodes.label: Experimental Paddle OCR
nodes.description: Included only by an explicit experimental build; startup/promotion gates have not passed and normal builds exclude it.

nodes.label: Reusable IndexedDB knowledge
nodes.description: IndexedDB v5 stores reusable site knowledge and parameterized saved routes separately from private active-session context; incompatible derived indexes rebuild.

nodes.label: Optional Fastify/SQLite mirror
nodes.description: Explicitly connected single-owner service mirrors reusable knowledge with v1 compatibility and v2 workflow/visual negotiation; browser authority and local fallback remain.

nodes.label: Pinned session identity
nodes.description: Session token, browser tab, document, protocol, and origin are pinned; back/forward and same-document history trigger fresh binding scans.

nodes.label: Chromium worker and Firefox event-page restoration
nodes.description: The Chromium service worker and Firefox event page restore privileged pinned state; current tab/document/session/origin validation and fresh observations survive suspension.

nodes.label: Session-scoped presentation visibility
nodes.description: Expanded, minimized, and hidden presentation are separate trusted state; suppressing overlays need not stop authorized observation or verification.

nodes.label: Pinned-tab command rejection
nodes.description: Guide/Get Page/Resume from another active tab are rejected; closing the pinned tab clears the active session while Stop/Pause can clear it from the panel.

nodes.label: MV3 lifecycle evidence
nodes.description: Chromium tests terminate the real worker and use a new test-only epoch; Firefox conformance terminates the real event page and checks rehydration plus fresh inference. These are repository contracts, not runs performed for this graph.

nodes.label: Authored Northstar regression routes
nodes.description: Two controlled versioned fixture packs use semantic landmarks, expected state transitions, exact origins, and explicit boundaries; they are separate from product live discovery.

nodes.label: Terminal irreversible-action boundary
nodes.description: Final irreversible authored actions have no outgoing transitions; login checkpoints and declared visible success evidence are distinct states.

nodes.label: Dynamic navigator.live mode
nodes.description: The worker exposes navigator.live version 1.0.0 for HTTP/HTTPS; it uses observations and goal plans rather than pretending to be an authored route graph.

nodes.label: Live/authored payload isolation
nodes.description: Live views require valid unique current visible/enabled control IDs; authored views reject generic page/control/goal payloads and both modes reject route/version substitution.

nodes.label: Structural heading and region context
nodes.description: Generic HTML/ARIA heading ancestry, named regions, enclosing sections, and document/shadow-root ownership distinguish repeated controls without site-specific selectors.

nodes.label: Generic context specificity
nodes.description: Extra qualifiers in a nearest section reduce rank; unknown scope remains unknown, structural changes invalidate signatures/revisions, and geometry is not model input.
nodes.rationale: Repeated control labels require semantic context without encoding website names or routes.

nodes.label: Experimental Chrome Prompt API interpretation
nodes.description: Opt-in local model proposes structured intent and current IDs from bounded sanitized evidence; it has no selector, action, or completion authority.

nodes.label: Retrieved current-control model view
nodes.description: Ranks requested purpose and terms, keeps discovered openers, and bounds model input to 96 controls and about 24,000 characters; cannot recover undiscovered controls.

nodes.label: Pristine cancellable model request
nodes.description: Each request clones and destroys a pristine Prompt API session with cancellation and a 30-second timeout; current task context includes up to eight verified interactions.

nodes.label: Independent model-intent grounding
nodes.description: Planner requires one eligible live route, matching current IDs and operation/control kind, user-sourced qualifiers, and retained consequential/unknown-effect boundaries.

nodes.label: Bounded English task interpretation
nodes.description: Compromise parses the entire validated English request with order, negation, corrections, and desired values; maximum 1,000 characters and three explicit tasks.

nodes.label: Compromise/BM25/MiniLM pipeline
nodes.description: Sanitized semantic metadata feeds BM25 and normalized mean-pooled MiniLM vectors alongside semantic/observed-route planning; current state is validated separately.

nodes.label: Versioned derived embedding cache
nodes.description: SHA-256 plus pinned model revision keys a global 10,000-entry derived cache that can rebuild independently of original knowledge.

nodes.label: Packaged CPU inference across browser hosts
nodes.description: Shared packaged q8 MiniLM workers with one CPU thread and local WASM run under a Chromium offscreen document or Firefox MV3 event page; neither requires a remote model.

nodes.label: Inference cancellation and unloading
nodes.description: Foreground work takes priority; Stop cancels pending inference and disposes the shared browser host. Current code releases idle OCR workers after 10 seconds and NLP/host after 30 seconds; natural-language.md still contains superseded two-minute wording.

nodes.label: Verified multi-task queue
nodes.description: Queue advances on requested observed results; search focus is intermediate, review blocks, Skip records skipped, Pause retains, and Stop cancels.

nodes.label: Request/document/scan revision guards
nodes.description: Plans carry identifiers tying asynchronous work to current request, document, and observation revision; changed scans replan from the original sentence.

nodes.label: Explicit observation activation
nodes.description: Discovery starts on Guide me or explicit page exploration; panel opening alone does not observe. Pause/Stop remove discovery/invalidation observers and Resume rescans.

nodes.label: Bounded value-free observation
nodes.description: Reads bounded labels, authored descriptions, roles, headings, form metadata, relationships, and interaction state; excludes editable values, passwords, OTPs, and raw HTML.

nodes.label: Authentication continuity without credential handling
nodes.description: Field metadata and bounded form context detect authentication; the objective survives credential/two-factor waiting without an expiry deadline, while the user authenticates.

nodes.label: Trusted private session context
nodes.description: Privileged WebExtensions storage.session retains active requests, supplied values, entities, unfinished journeys and task navigation ledger; private entities/vectors remain outside reusable knowledge.

nodes.label: Bounded reusable memory retention
nodes.description: Limits reusable memory to 50 sites, per-site 100 pages/120 states/30 templates/400 transitions, 100 saved routes, and 90-day access-time expiry; derived cache has 10,000 entries.

nodes.label: Forget/Clear knowledge controls
nodes.description: Observation stops before deletion; Forget removes a website and traversing routes, Clear removes knowledge/routes/indexes, uninstall removes extension-owned data, and failed mirror deletion is reported.

nodes.label: Editable-field and iframe OCR masks
nodes.description: Capture hides Tholi overlays and masks discovered editable fields including open-shadow fields plus every iframe rectangle, even when frame DOM guidance is authorized.

nodes.label: Trusted draft and conversation storage
nodes.description: Preferences/bounds are local; draft and at most 80 messages stay in trusted extension-session storage, separate from website and cloud. Widget commands are session/document bound.

nodes.label: Session-only mock website accounts
nodes.description: Website accounts are explicitly fake; name/email/onboarding live in browser-session storage, passwords are neither persisted nor transmitted, and sign-out clears the mock account.

nodes.label: Consent-gated website appearance storage
nodes.description: Host-only SameSite=Lax consent lasts 180 days; optional theme cookie requires appearance consent, withdrawal deletes it, and blocked cookies preserve in-memory usability.

nodes.label: Inactive allowlisted analytics boundary
nodes.description: No production provider is configured. Future consent-bound events may include only public page categories, downloads, and two fixed practice task IDs; arbitrary private/user text is excluded.

nodes.label: Bounded redacted local diagnostics
nodes.description: Diagnostic exports omit labels, goals, paths, raw DOM, and field values; authenticated screenshots/traces are not captured by default.

nodes.label: All observed/model evidence is untrusted
nodes.description: Page text, observations, stored knowledge, documented predictions, and model outputs never independently authorize action or completion; fresh eligibility and signatures are required.
nodes.rationale: Website evidence and model suggestions may be stale, malicious, or mistaken; authority remains in validated runtime contracts and observed results.

nodes.label: Explicit per-origin host access
nodes.description: Default hosts are English Wikipedia and local development; other HTTP/HTTPS sites require specific grants. DOM and screenshot permissions are distinct.

nodes.label: Trusted sender and document validation
nodes.description: Extension commands require extension-owned sender identity; content messages require assigned tab/frame/document and validated contracts; stale results cannot replace current documents/tasks.

nodes.label: Consequential and unknown-effect review
nodes.description: Default Guide leaves actions with the user. Optional assistance is restricted to fresh eligible ordinary menus and explicitly requested view choices; forms, credentials, links, final and unknown-effect actions remain manual. Heuristic risk is not proof of arbitrary server behavior.

nodes.label: Single-owner API protection
nodes.description: Loopback default, bearer token, explicit extension-origin CORS, and HTTPS for remote hosting guard an optional service whose credentials remain trusted and whose private payloads are unpersisted.

nodes.label: Pending native and signed-in acceptance
nodes.description: Synthetic Chromium and public Wikipedia evidence do not certify arbitrary sites; native Chrome access/accessibility, actual screen-reader speech, real Gemini Nano quality, and signed-in workflows remain separate acceptance.

nodes.label: Single background-owned session and journey
nodes.description: One mutable pinned session remains in the Chromium worker or Firefox event page. Routine cross-service work uses one queue; validated Pause/Stop bypass routine work to interrupt the same owner promptly.
nodes.rationale: Service extraction cannot introduce parallel session caches or competing journey owners.

nodes.label: Stable generated browser entrypoints
nodes.description: Build preserves worker.js, content.js, frame-agent.js, offscreen.js, inference.js, ocr-worker.js, sidepanel.js, and theme-page.js.

nodes.label: Content runtime and PageCoach facade
nodes.description: Top runtime and PageCoach orchestrate observation, binding, plan lifecycle, outcome verification, frame agents, and visual guidance.

nodes.label: Single session snapshot subscription
nodes.description: useSessionSnapshot owns one snapshot subscription and bounded fallback; controllers and features receive typed state/actions without duplicate inference or polling.

nodes.label: Privilege-free shared presentation
nodes.description: packages/ui owns Guide/Conversation, attention, composer, route nodes, Wayfinder, and responsive priority; accepts state/callbacks and cannot access Chrome, credentials, permissions, or outcome authority.

nodes.label: Extension guidance composition
nodes.description: Controller composes feature actions and dedicated hooks while sidebar-only privileged settings remain outside embedded shared presentation.

nodes.label: Revision-protected draft restoration
nodes.description: Local edit revisions and matching UI_SAVE acknowledgement protect typing from stale reads and replies; surface handoff can restore a clean draft without changing the journey.

nodes.label: Session-bound isolated widget shell
nodes.description: Closed-shadow shell owns clamped geometry/pointer capture and trusted typed layout actions; extension-origin iframe owns guidance and its Widget menu, with keyboard alternatives.

nodes.label: State-preserving widget density
nodes.description: Density depends on usable width/height with immediate reduction and buffered expansion; shared components stay mounted and draft, selection, and focus survive tier changes.

nodes.label: Isolated website practice adapter
nodes.description: Shadow-root embedded GuidanceApp consumes controlled sample outcomes and callbacks; the practice has no Chrome permissions or production journey ownership.

nodes.label: Recorded product media versus brand motion
nodes.description: Marketing consumes a genuine recording manifest; capture requires a real worker-verified public-page result and immutable hashes, while brand motion emits no journey/completion evidence.

nodes.label: Allowlisted safe website documentation
nodes.description: Lazy docs registry permits selected Markdown, local search and explicit reference aliases; raw HTML is disabled, images become source links, and initial Home avoids repository Markdown.

nodes.label: Website history and heading-aware routing
nodes.description: App router separates pathname/query/fragment, preserves modified clicks/Back/scroll, waits for lazy headings/fragments, and bounds/cancels observers and animation frames.

nodes.label: Passive geometry-bound guidance overlay
nodes.description: Closed-shadow overlay ignores pointer input and accessibility tree; one frame loop tracks the fresh target rectangle without decorative interpolation, clears hidden targets, and cancels on Pause/Stop.

nodes.label: Meaningful polite status and focus management
nodes.description: Panel supplies equivalent instruction/progress in one polite atomic region; polling/geometry do not repeat announcements, and Guide/Pause/Stop manage focus predictably.

nodes.label: Independent geometry and keyboard evidence
nodes.description: Browser tests independently inspect overlay geometry via CDP across movement/zoom/edges/reduced motion and check keyboard focus/status behavior; this does not prove native screen-reader speech.

nodes.label: Feature-local website ownership
nodes.description: App owns routing/history, SiteLayout navigation/footer, practice sample state, legal its canonical content/operator details, and docs stable public article aliases.

nodes.label: Stable public documentation aliases
nodes.description: Public article slugs survive repository moves through explicit legacy-reference aliases; historical evidence remains a repository link.

nodes.label: Offline local default
nodes.description: Packaged English MiniLM and Tesseract run locally on CPU with no cloud model/backend or user account required; optional Chrome/backend integrations remain separate opt-ins.

nodes.label: Deterministic PR validation gate
nodes.description: npm run test:ci builds once and validates deterministic PR behavior; focused existing checks guide implementation and prepared builds require immutable verified artifacts.

nodes.label: Same-run exact-byte release certification
nodes.description: Full-tier evidence must cover the final build before packaging. Do not rebuild afterward, overwrite existing archives, or aggregate focused historical reports as certification.
nodes.rationale: Independent or historical test evidence cannot certify different artifact bytes.

nodes.label: Frozen evaluation corpora
nodes.description: Original fixture bytes, splits, hashes, and thresholds are preserved; calibration needs explicit versioning/independent review and predictions cannot regenerate expectations.

nodes.label: Stable legacy compatibility identifiers
nodes.description: Product copy uses Tholi while scoped packages, storage keys, environment variables, and protocol identifiers retain legacy names for compatibility.

nodes.label: Pinned third-party model and discovery provenance
nodes.description: Bundled license texts and generated third-party.json describe pinned dependencies; MiniLM revision, adapted Playwright hashes, OCR assets, and experimental Paddle/OpenCV adaptations have explicit provenance.

nodes.label: Historical evidence versus current behavior
nodes.description: Versioned records describe specific tested bytes and are neither current installation instructions nor broad current reliability guarantees.
nodes.rationale: Evidence must remain attached to the tested version/build, with current behavior and pending acceptance stated separately.

nodes.label: Browser platform ownership
nodes.description: Shared engine with typed adapters, native document identity, separate target hosts/settings/sidebar/builds and target-specific evidence.

nodes.label: Typed WebExtensions platform boundary
nodes.description: Mozilla webextension-polyfill centralizes common APIs; Chromium-specific capabilities are detected in adapters.
nodes.rationale: Browser differences belong at the adapter boundary while navigation, privacy and acceptance contracts stay shared.

nodes.label: Mandatory native browser document identity
nodes.description: Native document IDs remain mandatory; URL-only or synthetic fallbacks cannot substitute for safety APIs.
nodes.rationale: Fail closed on missing safety capabilities instead of weakening stale-document protection.

nodes.label: Shared inference host for Chromium and Firefox
nodes.description: Chromium offscreen and Firefox event-page hosts use the same request/cancel/dispose contract and lazy NLP/OCR workers; no hidden-tab keepalive.
nodes.rationale: Preserve shared model settings, cancellation and budgets without parallel inference implementations.

nodes.label: Browser-specific protected settings
nodes.description: Chromium TRUSTED_CONTEXTS storage preserves keys; Firefox backend/vision settings live in extension-origin tholi-private-settings IndexedDB.
nodes.rationale: Content scripts must not gain backend credentials because one browser lacks Chromium storage access levels.

nodes.label: Native sidebar activation and safe docking
nodes.description: Maps sidePanel/sidebarAction, invokes activation before asynchronous work, retains widget after failed dock and validates session/document before removal.
nodes.rationale: Native UI activation and transport differences must not discard the only usable guidance surface.

nodes.label: Firefox widget snapshot subscription
nodes.description: Firefox embedded UI uses the existing runtime port instead of unavailable tab events; no second snapshot subscription.

nodes.label: Visible origin intent and fresh permission checks
nodes.description: Host permission requests begin in a genuine user gesture with visible origin intent and recheck active tab/origin after approval.
nodes.rationale: Prevent asynchronous permission approval from binding a task to a different active website.

nodes.label: Separate target manifests and artifacts
nodes.description: Common manifest derives Chromium dist/extension and Firefox dist/extension-firefox with event-page scripts, sidebar_action and stable Gecko ID.
nodes.rationale: Retain stable entrypoint filenames while producing independently attributable target artifacts.

nodes.label: Target-specific exact-artifact certification
nodes.description: Evidence identifies browser/version, target, run and artifact digest. Chromium evidence cannot certify Firefox artifacts.
nodes.rationale: Shared source does not establish equal behavior or certify another browser build.

nodes.label: Optional assisted navigation
nodes.description: Default-off assistance opens fresh ordinary disclosures or chooses explicitly requested view options; worker and content independently validate authority and binding.
nodes.rationale: Reduce repetitive menu steps without handing final actions, credential handling or completion authority to synthetic interaction.

nodes.label: Retained destination during scan recovery
nodes.description: Changing scans retain the destination and replan; pending indexing has bounded recovery while native document/session mismatch remains rejected.
nodes.rationale: Observation revision churn is recoverable within one authorized document and must not silently widen authority.

nodes.label: Foreground controls and workflow reconciliation
nodes.description: Main-content/open-menu context, selected navigation and live routes reduce duplicate choices; equal distinct destinations still need a user choice.
nodes.rationale: Use current state to avoid repeating intermediate steps while waiting for independently observed final effects.

nodes.label: Bounded observed-route timeout feedback
nodes.description: Idempotent timeouts reduce confidence only in already observed ordinary route edges; later verified success decays penalties and private destination content stays excluded.
nodes.rationale: Learn from a failed attempt without inventing a route, declaring impossibility or persisting private text.

nodes.label: Shared authentication phrase normalization
nodes.description: Interpretation and lexical retrieval share authentication aliases and punctuation normalization while protecting quoted names and URLs.
nodes.rationale: Natural sign-in/sign-up phrasing should agree across interpretation and retrieval without rewriting protected entities.

nodes.label: Bounded latest-context priority inference
nodes.description: Extension and API use the same bounded priority queue implementation. Each queue has one active CPU call and eight waiting requests; newest work replaces older work per document context and foreground planning cancels suggestions.
nodes.rationale: Bound resource use and discard stale delivery instead of running concurrent copies of the model.

nodes.label: Current idle worker release budgets
nodes.description: NLP workers release after 30 seconds; OCR after 10 seconds. The client releases the idle host after 30 seconds; one pending host startup/disposal is serialized.
nodes.rationale: Release heavy workers promptly without a late cleanup killing a resumed host.

nodes.label: Three-attempt scan recovery budget
nodes.description: Retries coalesce behind one in-flight plan; the recovery key follows request/task/verified progress/page rather than every fingerprint. Three retries pause checking with destination retained.
nodes.rationale: Continuous page mutations must not replenish retries indefinitely or lose the destination.

nodes.label: Pause and Stop bypass routine queued work
nodes.description: Validated Pause/Stop interrupt the same session owner directly; generation fences invalidate pending results rather than awaiting busy-page acknowledgment.
nodes.rationale: Users need a prompt way to halt observation and CPU work even while routine requests are queued.

nodes.label: Bounded 1,024-entry vector and hash caches
nodes.description: Hot vectors and content hashes are each capped at 1,024 entries, sufficient for one 600-control page projection and its query; disposal clears both.
nodes.rationale: A 512-entry provisional cache thrashed on 601 texts; this budget preserves reuse without unbounded private-text retention.

nodes.label: Masked foreground-region OCR
nodes.description: A visible actual foreground menu/dialog supplies an ephemeral bounded capture-space region; all privacy masks still apply across the full image.
nodes.rationale: Improve useful text evidence in layered interfaces without reducing image masking or conferring action authority.

nodes.label: Relevant mutations and owned-UI exclusion
nodes.description: Both scan paths exclude Tholi shadow roots. Incremental observation tracks control/accessibility references, ignores unrelated ticking text and clears reference state on teardown.
nodes.rationale: Prevent rendering the guide from recursively invalidating website discovery while preserving relevant control, receipt and accessibility changes.

nodes.label: Embedding tensor resource disposal
nodes.description: Each extracted embedding vector releases its temporary output tensor in finally, including invalid-vector paths.
nodes.rationale: Avoid retaining model output resources after the JavaScript vector has been copied.

Live planning and sidebar polls read cached committed knowledge rather than waiting for storage. Stalled IndexedDB transactions abort after five seconds, preserving previous knowledge. Forget/Clear and route deletion discard pending writes and drain the current writer before deletion, including optional backend mirroring. Derived embedding/index writes use the same background scheduling policy. A cache read that exceeds 200 ms falls back to CPU computation and briefly bypasses the unavailable cache; persistence cannot become an inference prerequisite. Worker errors and a 30-second request deadline settle outstanding calls and replace the worker rather than leaving Chrome message ports pending. Such errors never count as task completion.

# Tholi architecture and evidence tour

Tholi 0.11.0 is an unreleased local website guide with Chromium and Firefox targets. A person supplies a destination; Tholi interprets current website evidence, proposes a freshly bound next step and independently checks the result. Guide mode leaves actions with the person. A new default-off Assisted navigation setting can open eligible ordinary menus and select an explicitly requested view option. Neither synthetic nor human clicks establish arrival.

This study reads all 14 current architecture documents, the repository overview, contributor instructions, third-party notices and documentation index, and cross-checks changed platform, runtime, inference, assistance and discovery implementations. It compares revision `360f710` with the earlier 0.10.1 map. It is source analysis; browser, accessibility, signed-in acceptance and production certification were not performed for this graph.

## What changed since the earlier map

| Area | Earlier map | Current source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browsers | Chromium worker/offscreen ownership | Shared WebExtensions boundary; Chromium service worker/offscreen and Firefox MV3 event-page hosts |
| Browser identity | Chrome-specific examples | Native document identity is mandatory on both targets; missing safety APIs fail closed |
| Credentials | Trusted Chromium local storage | Chromium TRUSTED_CONTEXTS or Firefox extension-origin private IndexedDB |
| Guidance actions | Human performs website actions | Default remains Guide; explicit opt-in permits bounded ordinary disclosures and requested view choices |
| Scan churn | Replan on changed observation | Retained destination, coalesced in-flight work, bounded retries and pause on persistent churn |
| Navigation context | Structural headings and regions | Foreground/menu context, duplicate-destination grouping and live intermediate-stage reconciliation |
| Inference scheduling | Foreground preemption | Shared bounded queue implementation, eight waiting jobs, newest work per context and cancellation fences |
| Resource cleanup | Two-minute host cleanup | Current code: OCR workers 10 seconds, NLP workers and host 30 seconds; bounded hot caches and tensor disposal |
| Stop and Pause | Routine serialized session commands | Validated interrupts bypass routine queued work while using the same owner |
| OCR | Masked viewport fallback | Full-image masks plus an optional foreground menu/dialog pass and viewport fallback |
| Learned route confidence | Verified transition counts | Idempotent timeout penalty on existing ordinary edges, decayed by later verified success |

These are reliability and platform changes, not a cloud/SaaS conversion. The [current NLP architecture](../../docs/architecture/natural-language.md) explicitly leaves hosted inference, multi-user synchronization and multilingual requests deferred. MiniLM and Tesseract weights, single-thread settings, frozen inputs and consequential-action boundaries remain unchanged.

## Ownership stays coherent

| Owner | Responsibility | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background runtime | One pinned session and journey, permissions, hydration, memory, frame and vision coordination | [worker-runtime.ts](../../apps/extension/src/background/worker-runtime.ts) |
| Content runtime | Observation, fresh binding, plan lifecycle, verification and authorized assistance | [page-coach.ts](../../apps/extension/src/content/page-coach.ts), [plan-lifecycle.ts](../../apps/extension/src/content/plan-lifecycle.ts) |
| Navigation core | Validated requests, retrieval/planning, queues, workflows and continuity | [navigation-core](../../packages/navigation-core/index.ts) |
| Platform adapters | Typed APIs, browser capabilities, inference hosts, native sidebars and private settings | [browser platforms](../../docs/architecture/browser-platforms.md) |
| Shared UI | Presentation and callbacks; no permissions, credentials or completion authority | [shared UI](../../docs/architecture/frontend/shared-ui.md) |
| Website practice | Isolated controlled sample state using the real shared presentation | [website ownership](../../docs/architecture/frontend/website.md) |
| Optional API | Explicitly connected single-owner knowledge mirror, shared core and local fallback | [navigation architecture](../../docs/architecture/navigation.md) |

One queue still coordinates ordinary background work. Pause and Stop now use a validated interruption path to the same owner; this is not another session runtime. Shared UI and website practice do not acquire extension authority. Preserved filenames, storage keys, protocol identifiers, route versions and public document aliases remain compatibility boundaries.

## Two browser targets, one engine

The typed [API boundary](../../apps/extension/src/platform/api.ts) uses Mozilla webextension-polyfill. [Capability checks](../../apps/extension/src/platform/capabilities.ts) require scripting, native frame identity and session storage; Chromium additionally needs offscreen/context APIs, while Firefox needs worker support. Minimum engines are Chromium 140 and Firefox 153.

[Inference hosting](../../apps/extension/src/platform/inference-host.ts) creates a Chromium offscreen document or a Firefox-local instance of the same [worker host](../../apps/extension/src/inference/worker-host.ts). Workers are lazy, cancellable and disposable. Startup/disposal is serialized to prevent late cleanup from killing a resumed host. There is no hidden-tab or polling keepalive.

[Private settings](../../apps/extension/src/platform/private-settings.ts) preserve Chromium keys behind TRUSTED_CONTEXTS. Firefox uses extension-origin IndexedDB `tholi-private-settings` because it lacks that access-level API. Backend and vision settings stay outside content-script storage; private requests/drafts stay in privileged session storage. Separate browser installations do not synchronize knowledge.

[Sidebar adaptation](../../apps/extension/src/platform/sidebar.ts) respects genuine user activation. Failed Dock keeps the usable widget; removal follows native opening and fresh session/document validation. Firefox widget snapshots reuse the runtime port because embeds have a narrower API subset. A disconnected port is not proof of dismissal.

[Target manifests](../../config/extension-targets.mjs) keep Chromium output in `dist/extension` and Firefox in `dist/extension-firefox`, with stable Gecko ID `tholi@ilunonsen.com`. Target-specific run identities and artifact digests are required: Chromium evidence does not certify Firefox bytes.

## Optional assistance has two authorization gates

The pure [assistance policy](../../packages/safety-policy/assistance.ts) accepts an active task and visible, enabled, in-viewport, unoccluded, ordinary top-frame controls. It allows a closed menu/listbox/tree disclosure, or an exact requested choice among eligible radio/option/tab/select controls. Links, forms, credentials, committing or unknown effects and frame targets remain outside its authority.

The existing [UI hook](../../apps/extension/src/ui/hooks/useAssistance.ts) debounces a candidate for 400 milliseconds using the existing snapshot. The [worker transport](../../apps/extension/src/background/ui-transport.ts) validates the sender, opt-in setting, active tab, native document, session/request/revision/control identity and expanded surface. The content coach refreshes discovery, checks actual connected binding, clipping, sensitive ancestors and live policy, then limits attempts by request/state/signature. Its 64-entry attempt set bounds retained identifiers; it is not a guarantee that all page effects are known.

The implementation invokes synthetic interaction only after these checks. Existing observation and outcome verification decide what happened, including ignored clicks. This is a meaningful product capability, and it expands the need for negative regression coverage because risk classification remains heuristic.

## Recovery and resource budgets

[Plan lifecycle](../../apps/extension/src/content/plan-lifecycle.ts) retains intent while indexing and allows one automatic plan in flight. A recovery key follows request, active task, verified progress and page identity; changing fingerprints do not replenish the budget. Three bounded retries use exponential delay, then pause checking while preserving the destination. Native document/session rejection is separate and cannot be bypassed by scan recovery.

[Incremental discovery](../../packages/page-discovery/incremental.ts) excludes Tholi-owned roots and ignores unrelated ticking text while tracking relevant controls, foreground surfaces and referenced accessibility labels. Reference bookkeeping is cleared on stop. This prevents the guide's own rendering from recursively triggering website work. Fresh observations publish before asynchronous replanning.

The [inference queue](../../packages/nlp/work-queue.ts) has one active call and at most eight waiting requests per instance. The extension and API use the same implementation in their own runtimes. Foreground destinations/decisions outrank continuation and suggestions; newest work replaces older work in the same native context. Cancellation rejects stale delivery even when a CPU call must finish before reuse.

[MiniLM](../../packages/nlp/model.ts) disposes each output tensor in `finally`. [Retrieval](../../packages/nlp/retrieval.ts) bounds hot vectors and hashes to 1,024 entries each, enough for the 600-control projection plus query. These are transient hot caches, distinct from the 10,000-entry persistent derived cache. Current worker code releases idle OCR after 10 seconds, planning after 30 seconds, and the client releases the host after 30 seconds.

The [NLP document](../../docs/architecture/natural-language.md) still mentions a two-minute cleanup; that sentence is stale relative to code and the [October 19 performance record](../../docs/releases/v0.11.0/performance.md). This map records the discrepancy rather than treating both budgets as current.

## Evidence and privacy still constrain the planner

Current main-content, selected-route and foreground-menu evidence can reconcile intermediate workflow state and group duplicate links to the same destination. Genuinely different equally grounded destinations still need a user choice. Timed-out actions are bounded and excluded in the same state. Route confidence penalties apply only to already observed ordinary edges, never creating a route or proving one impossible.

The [visual guidance owner](../../apps/extension/src/content/visual-guidance.ts) can identify one foreground menu/dialog region, but full-image editable-field and iframe masking remains in force. Coordinates stay in original capture space and are temporary. DOM bindings take precedence; OCR text, confidence or changed pixels cannot establish task completion. Paddle remains experimental.

Private objectives, supplied values, entities, unfinished journeys, drafts and conversation stay session-only. Reusable knowledge stores sanitized structure, parameterized routes and observed transitions with existing retention/deletion budgets. Raw HTML, screenshots, private OCR text, coordinates and ephemeral control/document IDs stay outside reusable persistence. Sanitization and action-risk heuristics cannot promise perfect recognition on arbitrary websites. See [privacy](../../docs/architecture/privacy.md) and [security](../../docs/architecture/security.md).

## Assessment and outstanding evidence

The changes address real causes of unreliable guidance: repetitive intermediate steps, scan churn, uninterruptible queued work, stale suggestions and avoidable inference retention. The browser adapter boundary preserves the engine's identity across targets, and assistance reuses existing session and verification owners rather than introducing a second automation system. These are strong architectural improvements.

The remaining commercial uncertainty is live task reliability. Recorded targeted passes do not establish universal website correctness or certify a release. The [0.11.0 validation checklist](../../docs/releases/v0.11.0/validation.md) explicitly says not certified for packaging. The performance record keeps separate evidence cohorts, reports one held-out GitHub mismatch and long frames in the extreme 50,000-node scene, and leaves signed-in Amazon/Cloudflare/GitHub, native/manual, hosted-timing and weaker-CPU checks pending. Its metrics are reported repository evidence, not measurements rerun for this study.

Priority should remain representative user journeys, understandable recovery, prompt cancellation and independent outcomes. Firefox increases reach and also the browser acceptance matrix. Optional assistance increases convenience and also reliance on conservative action classification. Cloud models could later improve interpretation and visual understanding, but they would still need these local identity, eligibility, privacy and verification contracts.

## Reading and graph provenance

Start with [navigation](../../docs/architecture/navigation.md), [browser platforms](../../docs/architecture/browser-platforms.md), [sessions](../../docs/architecture/sessions.md), [natural language](../../docs/architecture/natural-language.md) and [page context](../../docs/architecture/page-context.md). Frontend responsibilities are in [the index](../../docs/architecture/frontend/README.md), [extension](../../docs/architecture/frontend/extension.md), [guidance](../../docs/architecture/frontend/guidance.md), [shared UI](../../docs/architecture/frontend/shared-ui.md) and [website](../../docs/architecture/frontend/website.md). [Authored regression routes](../../docs/architecture/authored-routes.md) remain isolated controlled fixtures.

[architecture.json](architecture.json) preserves existing concept IDs, adds verified 0.11.0 concepts and provides current line anchors. EXTRACTED edges use explicit source evidence at confidence 1.0. Interpretive implementation support is INFERRED and labeled `supported_by`; no import/call relationships are invented. Every `evidence_files` path was checked against this revision. Source links are relative to this checked-out snapshot and remain portable with the snapshot.

# Changes since the previous map

This rescan compares the previous source snapshot, `8c8b442`, with verified GitHub main revision `360f710` (Chromium firefox integration, PR 21). The commit changes 190 files, with 11,193 inserted and 3,224 removed lines, including committed evidence reports. The user's working checkout remains at the older revision. The new graph reads an isolated source snapshot, verified against Git blobs including permitted checkout line-ending conversion. Injected mapping tooling and reviewed graph material are identified separately in `graphify-out/rescan-revision.json` in the original workspace. This is a source study with focused structural checks, not fresh browser certification.

## One engine across Chromium and Firefox

The previous map described a Chrome extension with Chrome-specific lifecycle and offscreen inference. The new source introduces a typed WebExtensions boundary, browser capabilities, platform-owned sidebar and inference hosts, and browser-specific handling of privileged settings. Chromium continues using a service worker and offscreen document; Firefox uses an event page and shared worker host. Both retain one pinned session owner and mandatory native document identity.

`apps/extension/src/platform/api.ts`, `capabilities.ts`, `sidebar.ts`, `inference-host.ts`, and `private-settings.ts` are the relevant owners. Firefox backend/vision settings use extension-origin IndexedDB because it lacks Chromium's local-storage access-level API. The adapter rejects missing capabilities rather than substituting URL-only identity. Sidebar handoff and permission requests explicitly respect user activation and validate the session/document after asynchronous work.

Normal builds produce Chromium and Firefox targets. `config/extension-targets.mjs` retains the existing entrypoint filenames while deriving target manifests. The documented minimums are Chromium 140 and Firefox 153. Firefox is an unsigned temporary developer preview that disappears on browser restart. Other branded browsers have their own evidence requirements; compatibility is not universal native verification.

Sources: [browser platform architecture](../../docs/architecture/browser-platforms.md), [target definition](../../config/extension-targets.mjs), [browser support record](../../docs/releases/v0.10.1/browser-support.md).

## Optional assisted navigation changes the action boundary

The new assistance setting is off by default. It can reveal eligible menus and select an explicitly requested ordinary view option. This is an actual execution capability: content may perform a synthetic click or set a native select and dispatch its input/change events.

The worker checks trusted UI identity, opt-in preference, active pinned tab, native top-document identity, visible expanded surface, current task/control and observation revision. Content checks the fresh bound element, visibility, viewport, occlusion, active task and review/authentication state. The shared policy rejects nonordinary risk, consequential labels, frame targets and unsupported operations. Content excludes links, forms, editable contexts, sensitive elements, submit/reset controls and ordinary text inputs. Attempts are deduplicated by request, observed state and target signature.

These gates narrow the capability. Risk classification remains heuristic, and websites may ignore synthetic events. The synthetic interaction itself supplies no success evidence: existing observations and task-specific verification determine whether anything happened. Default manual guidance remains available.

Source owners: `packages/safety-policy/assistance.ts`, `apps/extension/src/background/ui-transport.ts`, `apps/extension/src/content/page-coach.ts`, `apps/extension/src/ui/hooks/useAssistance.ts`. See [assistance controls and limits](../../docs/guides/using-tholi.md#optional-assisted-navigation).

## Recovery and planning target actual friction

The current lifecycle retains the destination through transient scan changes instead of immediately returning the previous page-change error. It permits one automatic plan in flight, coalesces later work, and limits stale-scan recovery across changing fingerprints. Repeated invalidation pauses checking with the objective retained. Recovery budgets reset for meaningful context/progress changes rather than every ticking fingerprint.

Shared text normalization improves sign-up/sign-in wording and Unicode punctuation while protecting quoted names and URLs. `packages/navigation-core/screen-context.ts` reconciles selected navigation against actual live destinations, prioritizes foreground surfaces and deduplicates equivalent destination controls. These checks reduce already-open menu/sidebar loops without converting a matching label into arrival evidence.

Observed route feedback now reduces confidence in an existing verified edge after a timeout. It cannot create an edge. Feedback IDs make application idempotent within a bounded retained history; later verified success reduces the failure penalty. The route planner incorporates that penalty in its existing cost calculation.

Sources: [navigation reliability record](../../docs/releases/v0.11.0/navigation-reliability.md), `apps/extension/src/content/plan-lifecycle.ts`, `packages/goal-planner/task-intent.ts`, `packages/navigation-core/screen-context.ts`, `packages/site-memory/index.ts`, `packages/goal-planner/route-graph.ts`.

## Scheduling, observation and memory are more deliberate

`packages/nlp/work-queue.ts` gives explicit user requests priority over automatic continuation and suggestions. Its bounded queue holds up to eight pending jobs, replaces stale context, aborts canceled work and keeps CPU model calls serialized. An active call still must settle before the next CPU call starts. Pause and Stop bypass routine worker queues, invalidate generations and clear observation/inference without waiting for a busy content acknowledgment.

Discovery excludes Tholi-owned shadow roots and suppresses unrelated ticking text while retaining meaningful control, modal, receipt and referenced accessibility changes. This addresses observation/replanning feedback loops caused by the product's own UI. MiniLM disposes output tensors; discovery caches clear on teardown. Hot vectors and content hashes are bounded at 1,024 entries each. That working set accommodates the 600-control projection and active query; it is distinct from the persistent derived cache.

The implementation releases idle OCR workers after 10 seconds and NLP/host resources after 30 seconds. The current `docs/architecture/natural-language.md` still mentions a two-minute idle timer; that sentence is stale relative to `apps/extension/src/inference/client.ts`, `worker-host.ts`, and the new performance record. The map records this documentation mismatch rather than repeating it as current behavior.

OCR can focus recognition on a foreground menu/dialog after full-image masking, with viewport fallback. Editable fields and all frame pixels stay masked. The same bundled MiniLM/Tesseract weights, single-thread settings and safety budgets remain. A larger hosted model or cloud crawler has not been introduced.

Sources: [performance follow-up](../../docs/releases/v0.11.0/performance.md), `packages/nlp/work-queue.ts`, `packages/nlp/model.ts`, `packages/nlp/retrieval.ts`, `packages/page-discovery/incremental.ts`, `apps/extension/src/inference/worker-host.ts`, `apps/extension/src/content/visual-guidance.ts`.

## Versioning and evidence now cover both targets

The source is 0.11.0, unreleased. Root, bundled workspaces, extension and API metadata are synchronized. `scripts/version.mjs` checks metadata, local dependency pins, lockfile entries, release notes and version tags. `scripts/verify-full.mjs` and packaging require target-specific evidence; a Chromium report cannot certify Firefox artifacts. Downloads continue to identify their actual eligible archive version, and older recording provenance remains unchanged.

The records distinguish several evidence cohorts:

| Cohort | Recorded scope | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-version navigation v5 | 394 PR cases, 32 model/OCR cases and one paired performance experiment | Passing historical checks on 0.10.1 artifact bytes |
| Initial 0.11.0 version checks | 294 unit cases, types, versioning and builds | Focused evidence after metadata changes |
| October 19 performance v3 | 400 PR cases, plus 32 model/OCR cases and one paired experiment | Broader passing cohort before the final cache adjustment |
| Final v4 cache adjustment | 299 units, 32 model/OCR cases and one paired experiment, plus types/builds | Targeted final-change evidence; not a repeat of the entire full gate |

The final performance record reports Chrome/Firefox warm planning p95 of 129/166 ms, warm OCR p95 of 660/649 ms, Pause of 13/15 ms and Stop of 6/20 ms on the stated laptop. Cold planning remains 1,750/1,500 ms. These are recorded local samples, not measurements performed by this rescan or promises for every machine.

The 50,000-node scene still reports long frames: 250/233 ms with Tholi active and 267/217 ms stopped. Those ordered samples do not establish a causal speedup. Signed-in workflows, remaining native/manual checks, hosted timing and complete final-byte certification remain pending. The GitHub connector returned no workflow runs for this exact commit during this review; no hosted pass is asserted.

Sources: [version release notes](../../docs/releases/v0.11.0/README.md), [validation status](../../docs/releases/v0.11.0/validation.md), [performance record](../../docs/releases/v0.11.0/performance.md), [release procedure](../../docs/development/releasing.md).

## Assessment

My confidence in the local product's direction has increased. Recovery from changing screens, immediate cancellation and restrained memory use address problems a user feels on every journey. The browser adapters preserve a shared engine and make Firefox support an explicit capability contract. Separate target evidence and synchronized versioning improve release discipline.

Assisted navigation is the largest change to the trust boundary. Keeping it opt-in, restricting eligible actions and preserving independent outcome verification are good design decisions. Real workflow validation is especially important now that the application can execute limited interactions. A risk heuristic and a synthetic fixture cannot prove arbitrary website effects.

The work also adds maintenance scope: two runtime targets, more native browser harnesses and more evidence cohorts. The remaining priority is a clean coordinated final-byte full run and observed success with real users on a narrow supported set of workflows. Long-frame behavior and signed-in compatibility need continued attention.

This revision strengthens the offline/local product. OpenRouter/Gemini integration, production user accounts, subscription billing, multi-tenant storage and a deployed cloud service are not implemented by this commit. Website accounts remain explicitly mocked. The existing optional API remains a single-owner service. A hosted offering would build on this foundation, with its value still determined by reliable outcomes and customer demand.
